reason: Bile and lipase are shown acting on dietary fat.
expectation: The fat will be broken down into smaller components suitable for absorption.

effect: The fat became fatty acids and monoglycerides, completing the digestion goal. The result also clarified that bile disperses fat while lipase breaks it apart.
reaction: The distinction between bile and lipase was useful and satisfying to see.

mostWorthwhile.text: Breaking starch down in two stages was worthwhile: the shorter chains followed by individual glucose molecules made the progression toward absorption clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the three organs was straightforward but somewhat repetitive. Their roles became clearer only after the last fitting.

surprise.text: I found the explicit distinction between bile dispersing fat and lipase breaking it apart helpful; the picture description alone did not fully explain their different roles.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary: the named slots and ingredient descriptions gave each choice a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter to see how the digestion products cross the intestinal lining and reach the body. This chapter made those products clear, but stopped before absorption.
